hero.headline: Indian River County rental costs reach $1,222 for one-bedroom apartments
hero.teaser: New federal data shows Indian River County residents face average Fair Market Rent of $1,222 for a one-bedroom apartment, placing the Treasure Coast between affordable rural areas and expensive coastal markets.
hero.body:
Indian River County residents face a Fair Market Rent of $1,222 for a one-bedroom apartment, according to 2026 data released by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development. This figure positions Indian River County in the mid-range of South Florida rental markets, higher than more affordable rural areas like Okeechobee County at $1,032 but substantially lower than premium markets in the region.

HUD's Fair Market Rent data shows significant price variations across South Florida counties. Belle Glade in Palm Beach County offers the lowest rates at $890 for a one-bedroom, while Wellington in Palm Beach County has the highest at $2,850. The data reflects current market conditions based on surveys, rental listings and market adjustments. These figures serve as benchmarks for housing assistance programs but do not impose rent control limits on landlords. St. Lucie and Martin areas fall between Indian River and Wellington, with rates of $1,467 for one-bedroom apartments.

Real estate professionals point to several factors driving these disparities. Talbot Sutter, president of Sutter and Nugent Real Estate, attributes Wellington's premium pricing to quality amenities and location advantages. "A lot of it has to do with school districts, especially Wellington. They have like top A-rated schools, lifestyle, they have so many aspects from equestrian to outdoor activities," Sutter said. He noted that demand for properties with more acreage and land has increased even in the rental market, particularly in wealthy enclaves like Wellington, western Lake Worth, Delray Beach and Boca Raton. Sutter's clients often include executives from New York City seeking luxury rentals before purchasing homes.

For renters navigating South Florida's challenging market, Sutter recommends conducting thorough research before committing to a lease. "Know the market, do your comps. You have to really, really know the area if you don't want to get ripped off paying rent," he said. Residents throughout the region report difficulty affording housing as rental prices continue climbing faster than income growth. The rental disparities highlight broader housing affordability challenges affecting South Florida communities across various income levels.

cards.headline: Florida Judicial Qualifications Commission investigates 4th Circuit Judge for bench comments to litigants
cards.body:
The Florida Judicial Qualifications Commission has determined there is probable cause to investigate Circuit Court Judge Eric Roberson of the Florida 4th Judicial Circuit over allegedly inappropriate statements he made while presiding over cases. Roberson, who was appointed by Gov. Rick Scott and elected without opposition two years ago, is now facing scrutiny for his courtroom comments in multiple matters.

In the case of Zoe Wood v. Tatyana Ussin, Roberson allegedly told the respondent: "This is scary, there's something seriously off with you and it's a shock that there haven't been criminal charges for this. Part of me wants to ban you from ever coming back to our state, and keep your issues up in Virginia." The ruling in that case was successfully appealed, and a different judge was assigned to rehear it. In Taheshanoel Knight v. Matthew Kepp, the JQC says Roberson determined the petitioner lacked evidence to support her stalking allegations against the respondent. According to the commission, Roberson made comments to the petitioner about mental health issues and her name, stating that the court would eventually stop her from filing in the system.

The most serious allegations involve the case of Sylverter Greene v. Erika Greene-Raines. The JQC says Roberson called the petitioner "an entitled little snot" and told the respondent: "You are a terrible human being, and I can look you in the eye and tell you that. And I'm a judge, so that's a legal judgment, you are a terrible human being." The commission also alleges Roberson made remarks about the respondent's lack of violence while making comments that encouraged additional conflict between the parties. Roberson granted a permanent injunction against the respondent in this case and noted it was only his third such injunction that year, comparing the respondent to a previous respondent who had been a child molester.

Roberson has 20 days from June 11 to respond in writing to the JQC's findings. He has not responded to attempts to reach him at his office or cell phone, nor did he provide comment to Florida Politics about the allegations. When appointed nine years ago, Roberson, a former prosecutor in the same circuit, stated he would transition from an advocate's role to serving as a neutral arbiter. The JQC's findings suggest his conduct in these cases may not reflect that commitment to judicial neutrality.

cards.headline: Wrongful death lawsuit filed in St. Lucie County fatal Turnpike crash involving semi-truck driver
cards.teaser: A wrongful death lawsuit was filed Thursday months after a fatal crash on Florida's Turnpike that killed three people, when a semi-truck driver made an illegal U-turn in St. Lucie County.
cards.body:
A wrongful death lawsuit was filed following a fatal crash on Florida's Turnpike in St. Lucie County. On Aug. 12, 2025, at approximately 2:57 p.m., commercial truck driver Harjinder Singh attempted an illegal U-turn through a median crossover near Mile Marker 171. The crossover was clearly marked "U-TURN OFFICIAL USE ONLY," according to court documents. A minivan driven by Herby Dufresne, carrying passengers Rodrigue Dor and Faniola Joseph, struck the left side of the trailer in what the complaint describes as "a classic and fatal underride crash." All three occupants were killed, with Joseph pronounced dead at the scene.

The lawsuit, filed by an attorney representing the estate of victim Faniola Joseph, names multiple defendants including truck driver Harjinder Singh, trucking company White Hawk Carriers Inc., freight broker C.H. Robinson Company Inc., and company manager Harpreet Singh. The complaint alleges White Hawk Carriers had a documented unsafe federal safety record before C.H. Robinson selected the company, including a prior reportable crash on approximately Dec. 9, 2024, roadside inspection citations for unsafe driving violations, and repeated hours-of-service violations. C.H. Robinson, described as one of the largest transportation brokers in the United States with headquarters in Eden Prairie, Minnesota, is accused of selecting the carrier despite its documented safety issues. The lawsuit seeks damages exceeding $75,000 under Florida's Wrongful Death Act.

cards.headline: Lawsuit challenges Florida property tax amendment ballot language as misleading
cards.teaser: A voter advocacy group and two registered voters filed a lawsuit Thursday challenging the property-tax amendment ballot language Florida lawmakers approved for November.
cards.body:
A lawsuit filed Thursday in Leon County challenges the property-tax amendment Florida lawmakers approved for the November ballot. The complaint, filed by a voter advocacy group and two registered voters, argues the ballot language is "biased" and "misleading," accusing lawmakers of using campaign-style phrases like "Save Our Homes From Excessive Property Taxes," "protecting small businesses" and "ensuring fairness." The plaintiffs say the summary overstates the proposal by suggesting it guarantees funding for core services, fully eliminates non-school homestead taxes and immediately exempts the first $250,000 of a home's value, when the filing argues the initial exemption would be $150,000 in 2027. The lawsuit asks a judge to declare the wording unconstitutional and order Attorney General James Uthmeier to rewrite it within 10 days.

On June 2, lawmakers passed legislation to raise the homestead exemption for homeowners to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028 and create a framework for full exemption over time. Attorney Jamie Cole, representing the plaintiffs, argues the ballot language sounds like political advertising rather than a neutral summary. "A ballot amendment is supposed to be fair, neutral, and not biased, and it's supposed to be accurate," Cole said. Cole successfully challenged a similar property-tax amendment in 2007 when a judge found the ballot language for a proposed "Super Exemption" misleading. The amendment will appear on the November 2026 General Election Ballot and requires approval from at least 60 percent of voters to become law.

cards.headline: Oxbridge Academy hires Mike Colee as head football coach, roster numbers already growing
cards.body:
The Oxbridge Academy Thunderwolves football program has turned to new leadership as head coach Mike Colee takes the reins. Though only a few weeks into his role, Colee has already begun reshaping the team's roster. He acknowledged that when he arrived, the program faced lower enrollment numbers since families had already made summer plans before his involvement. However, the situation has shifted since he engaged with parents and students and released the schedule. "Once I got in there, once I got to meet with the parents, meet with the kids, get the schedule out there, we've been growing our numbers ever since," Colee said.

The new coach's approach is already resonating with players as the season approaches. Senior Cayden Pribramski highlighted Colee's emphasis on mental toughness and his ability to maximize each player's individual strengths. Rather than imposing a rigid system, Colee tailors his coaching to suit his athletes. "He's not the kind of guy to go out there and say, 'my way or the highway.' He's going to really build the stuff around you and help you to succeed," Pribramski explained. The senior believes this flexible approach will be key to the team's immediate success and long-term development as a program.

The Thunderwolves are determined to move forward after a challenging 0-11 campaign last season. Senior Brady Basis expressed the team's commitment to maintaining momentum as they prepare for the upcoming season. "We just want to keep working, keep going," Basis said. He pointed to a successful spring win as evidence that the team can build on positive performances. The goal is to carry that energy and winning mentality into the regular season.

Colee's appointment represents a significant turning point for Oxbridge Academy football. With improving roster numbers and players responding positively to his coaching philosophy, the program appears poised for change. The combination of increased participation and a coach who understands how to develop individual talent suggests the Thunderwolves are ready to compete under this new direction. As the team prepares to take the field, they're looking to prove themselves and leave last year's struggles behind.

cards.headline: Humane Society thrift stores in Stuart house cats during Palm City shelter renovation
cards.body:
The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast is making creative use of its thrift stores to maintain animal care operations while undergoing major construction at its Palm City shelter. The nonprofit started building upgrades to its adoption, customer service, and intake areas earlier this year, and many of the organization's cats have been temporarily relocated to the two retail locations. According to spokesperson Sarah Fisher, this arrangement has proven essential while the shelter's regular cages remain unavailable during the renovation project.

The shift has transformed the thrift stores into dual-purpose spaces where visitors can browse donated merchandise while also meeting cats available for adoption. Senior Manager Kelly Ellis emphasized that every purchase made at either location directly supports the animals in the organization's care. The stores welcome donations of gently used items from the community, giving shoppers a way to contribute to both the animal rescue mission and the renovation efforts simultaneously. This approach has created an unexpected benefit by bringing adoptable pets into spaces where community members shop regularly.

Beyond the cats staying at the thrift store locations, the Humane Society is actively recruiting temporary foster homes for other animals affected by the construction. This multi-pronged approach allows the organization to continue its full range of services even as the facility undergoes necessary improvements. Animal shelters across the country face similar challenges when buildings require upgrades, but the Treasure Coast shelter's strategy demonstrates how creative problem-solving can maintain community engagement while addressing infrastructure needs.

The two thrift stores are located at 3302 SE Federal Highway in Stuart and 1099 NW 21st St, also in Stuart. Anyone interested in shopping, donating items, or learning about foster opportunities can visit hstc1.org for store hours and donation guidelines. Fisher noted that the stores have become a lifeline for the animals during this renovation period, allowing the nonprofit to continue its mission without interruption despite the temporary limitations on shelter space.

hero.headline: Sara Baxter drops congressional bid, reenters Palm Beach County Commission race after Trump post
hero.teaser: Mayor Sara Baxter is dropping her congressional bid and reentering the Palm Beach County Commission race after President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social tha.
hero.body:
Mayor Sara Baxter is dropping her congressional bid and reentering the Palm Beach County Commission race after President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that he would prefer she remain on the commission. Baxter confirmed the decision exclusively to WPTV reporter Michael Hoffman, saying her initial run for Congress was motivated by her desire to help more people in her community. "With this new district and living in it, it was kind of one of those lifetime opportunities," Baxter said. "I want to be able to help residents and help more of them."

Trump, who had endorsed Baxter's campaign to stay on the county commission, posted on Truth Social Thursday night expressing his preference that she remain on the commission rather than run for Congress. "Sara Baxter is a fantastic person, and highly qualified for many top political jobs but, on a somewhat selfish basis, I would rather have her stay on the Palm Beach County Commission (where so many important things are happening!), than run for Congress. Thank you Sara!" Trump said. In a statement to Hoffman on Thursday night, Baxter said, "Just had the honor of speaking with President Donald Trump on the phone tonight. I'm grateful for his tremendous leadership and I'm proud to consider him a true friend. There's more work ahead, and I'm ready to keep serving the people of Palm Beach County. Let's get to it."

cards.headline: Palm Beach County shoppers switch to frozen produce as fresh fruit and vegetable prices climb 6%
cards.teaser: Palm Beach County shoppers are changing how they buy groceries as fresh fruit and vegetable prices climbed more than 6% over the past year, according to Thursday's federal inflation report and new consumer research.
cards.body:
Palm Beach County shoppers are changing their grocery habits as fresh fruit and vegetable prices have climbed more than 6% over the past year, according to Thursday's federal inflation report and research from financial services company Advance America. The Advance America study found that one in three American families now purchase fewer fresh fruits and vegetables due to rising costs, while 20% have switched to frozen alternatives. One Palm Beach County shopper who made the switch to frozen produce said the quality remains the same and organic options are available at comparable prices to fresh produce. Florida residents now spend over $28 more monthly on groceries compared to previous periods, with overall grocery prices increasing 2.7% year-over-year through May.

Some shoppers are expanding their grocery routines to find better deals on fresh produce. One Palm Beach County resident described visiting multiple stores, including Don Victor's in Lake Worth, to purchase vegetables, making his shopping day consist of two or three stops. Not all consumers are dramatically altering their habits. Another shopper said rising prices are manageable since they shop only for one person most of the time and continue buying fresh produce in moderate quantities.

cards.headline: Curaçao soccer team trains at Florida Atlantic University in Boca Raton before World Cup debut
cards.teaser: Hundreds of soccer fans filled Florida Atlantic University stadium in Boca Raton on Thursday to witness history as Curaçao prepares to make its first-ever World Cup appearance this weekend.
cards.body:
Hundreds of soccer fans gathered at Florida Atlantic University stadium in Boca Raton on Thursday to watch Curaçao's national team, known as the "Blue Wave," hold a training session ahead of the nation's first-ever World Cup appearance. Goalkeeper Eloy Room told WPTV that the support energized the team. "Really joyful to see that so many people showed up today. It gives us energy. We're really excited to start the World Cup," Room said. The island nation, with a population of just over 150,000 people, is the smallest nation to qualify for the tournament and went undefeated in all 10 of its 2026 World Cup qualifying matches.

Fans traveled across South Florida for the event, with some Curaçao natives driving from as far as Port St. Lucie. Marionella Barzeycoggins, originally from Curaçao, said she made sure her family attended. "I found out they're gonna be in Boca and they have a training event. And I'm like, oh my God, I have to RSVP so we are here. I'm super excited about that and I'm able to bring my whole family," Barzeycoggins said. Midfielder Tahitch Chong told WPTV the moment carries enormous meaning for the entire island. Curaçao faces Germany on Sunday in Houston, Texas.

More than 840 children have registered to play with the Wellington Soccer Club for the upcoming season, a record turnout that coaches and organizers attribute to growing World Cup excitement across South Florida. At Greenview Shores Park, boys and girls are training with their sights set on the sport's biggest stage. Nine-year-old Parker has his sights set on going pro like Argentinian soccer star Tadeo Allende, who now plays for Inter Miami. "I want to be like Allende when I grow up, he's my favorite player," Parker said.

Patrick Zoete, the club's director of coaching, has taught the sport for more than 25 years. He said soccer offers young players far more than athletic development. "Soccer provides not only exercise but also a way of life for the kids to be part of a team, camaraderie. Some of them remain friends for life," Zoete said. As the World Cup approaches, the Wellington Soccer Club is experiencing its biggest registration turnout yet. Zoete said the surge in interest is a pattern that repeats every four years. "We're fortunate that we have Messi here at Inter Miami. We can go watch the best player in the world," Zoete said. The Wellington Soccer Club is one of many organizations across the area experiencing the spike.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie police drones locate missing autistic woman on first day of testing
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie's Drone as First Responder program achieved immediate success during its first day of testing and evaluation on Wednesday, locating a missing autistic woman near a canal before officers arrived on scene. Police received a report of an autistic female walking through a wooded area adjacent to a canal bank. A DFR drone was remotely deployed from the police department and reached the scene faster than responding officers, quickly identifying both the missing woman and the person who reported her. Drone operators kept visual contact with both individuals and relayed their exact location to responding officers, enabling a safe reunion with her family. Police Chief Leo Niemczyk emphasized the program's immediate impact, stating "This program is about saving lives, and on day one, that's exactly what it helped us do." He added that "the successful location of a vulnerable autistic female near a canal before officers arrived demonstrates the tremendous value this technology brings to our community."

The agency completed 17 missions during the first day of operations. Beyond the missing person case, drones responded to several other emergency situations. They provided aerial surveillance during a burglary in progress, monitoring the area while officers approached and cleared the residence. During a domestic violence investigation, a drone arrived before patrol officers and spotted a suspect hiding in a backyard, providing real-time video feed to responding officers and supervisors. The drones also responded to multiple disturbance calls involving groups of minors, helping officers assess the situations and determine appropriate responses.

The DFR program integrates directly with the police department's computer-aided dispatch system. When emergency calls come in, trained personnel remotely launch drones from the station, placing surveillance on scene before officers arrive. In most cases, drones reach locations within seconds, with the longest travel time in the coverage area being approximately four minutes. Each drone operates for an average of 25 to 35 minutes per flight, depending on weather conditions. Currently, three drone docks are active as part of the testing phase, with plans to expand to six docks positioned throughout the city once the program becomes fully operational.

The DFR team consists of 12 specially trained officers. Police say drones may be deployed for active threats, burglaries, robberies, shootings, kidnappings, barricaded subjects, school emergencies, felony traffic stops, fleeing suspects, locating missing people, vehicle crashes, hazardous materials incidents, fires, and traffic monitoring. Chief Niemczyk noted that "technology will never replace our officers. But when technology allows us to locate a vulnerable person faster, improve officer safety, and provide better service to our residents, it's an investment worth making."

cards.headline: Hundreds of fish found dead in Port St. Lucie's Sawgrass Lakes after city algae treatment
cards.teaser: Dead fish were floating on top of the water at the Sawgrass Lakes community on Thursday in Port St. Lucie, after an algae treatment earlier in the week.
cards.body:
Dead fish were floating on top of the water at the Sawgrass Lakes community in Port St. Lucie on Thursday following an algae treatment the city conducted earlier in the week. Neighbors reached out to WPTV Thursday morning, sharing video of dead fish found in their backyards. "There were hundreds and hundreds of fish here, and thousands of those little ones just gulping the air," said neighbor Jim Herbert. On Tuesday and Wednesday, the city hired a vendor called SOLitude to treat the water for algae. Experts told WPTV that with high heat and algae treatment combined, the water can become uninhabitable for aquatic life. On Thursday, crews were in the neighborhood removing the dead fish and testing the oxygen levels in the water.

Scott Samples with the city of Port St. Lucie said the city has been working with neighbors and other cities and counties to find solutions. Jim Moir, executive director of the Indian Riverkeeper, said the city should look at more natural solutions, like planting aquatic vegetation, reducing the use of fertilizer, and removing sediment that can fuel algae growth. "We're going to end up in a cycle that we can't break unless we go back to square one and start with a natural remediation," said Moir. Herbert said this is at least the second time since he has lived in the Sawgrass Lakes community that there has been a fish die-off.

A rare Titan Arum, also known as the corpse flower and nicknamed "Princess Pungent," is set to bloom at McKee Botanical Garden in Vero Beach. According to the garden's Instagram tracking, the flower could bloom within the next few days or weeks. During its bloom period, which typically lasts only 24 to 48 hours, the flower emits the stench of rotting flesh, which explains its distinctive name. The plant is native to the rainforests of Sumatra and Indonesia and is considered endangered.

This particular Titan Arum arrived at McKee Botanical Garden in May 2026. In a Thursday update, the botanical garden reported the flower has grown nine inches taller, and one of its three remaining leaves has dropped, indicating bloom time is approaching. McKee Botanical Garden's annual Waterlily Celebration takes place June 13, potentially offering visitors the opportunity to see and smell the full bloom.

cards.headline: Humane Society of the Treasure Coast thrift stores in Stuart support shelter renovations
cards.teaser: The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast is using its two thrift stores to keep animal care going during a major renovation of its shelter in Palm City.
cards.body:
The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast is using its two thrift stores to sustain animal care during a major renovation of its shelter in Palm City. The nonprofit began construction on its adoption, customer service, and intake areas earlier this year, temporarily shifting many of its cats to store locations, according to spokesperson Sarah Fisher. "With our shelter cages unavailable, the stores have become a lifeline for our animals," Fisher said Thursday.

Senior Manager Kelly Ellis said shoppers can now find adoptable cats alongside unique items for sale at both thrift stores. "Every treasure you find here helps provide for our animals," Ellis noted, welcoming donations of gently used goods. The organization is currently seeking temporary foster homes for other animals while construction continues. The thrift stores are located at 3302 SE Federal Highway in Stuart and 1099 NW 21st St, Stuart. Store hours and donation guidelines are available at hstc1.org.

cards.headline: Martin County Commissioner calls for Brightline station move from downtown Stuart
cards.teaser: Martin County Commissioner Ed Ciampi called on county staff to open discussions with Brightline leadership about potentially moving the planned train station aw.
cards.body:
Martin County Commissioner Ed Ciampi called on county staff to open discussions with Brightline leadership about potentially moving the planned train station away from its previously agreed-upon downtown Stuart location. Ciampi said the current site, a parking lot across from the courthouse in downtown Stuart, creates parking issues and other problems. He suggested revisiting the fairgrounds as an alternative location. His comments came after the FEC sent a letter to then-Stuart mayor Christopher Collins stating it does not support a Brightline station in Stuart, saying the proposed station violates U.S. Coast Guard rules because it would require the St. Lucie River Railroad bridge to be down while the train stops at the station. Ciampi said if the station is deemed too close by the Army Corps of Engineers or the U.S. Coast Guard, it comes off the table for him, and moving it further south to the fairgrounds would eliminate that issue entirely.

Community members had mixed reactions to the commissioner's suggestion. Resident Paul Gedwed called it a well-thought-out opinion because there is congestion in the proposed location. Steven Vitale, owner of the Colorado Inn, disagreed, stating most people want to go downtown and questioning why they would build a train station people cannot walk to. Lisa Freitas, owner of Lisa Gay Fashion, said her store will benefit regardless of location and urged officials to get it done as long as it stays in Martin County. The county said Ciampi's comments are not official direction for staff. The topic would need board discussion and a vote before staff can explore a new location.

cards.headline: Lawsuit challenges Florida property tax amendment ballot language as misleading
cards.teaser: A voter advocacy group and two registered voters filed a lawsuit Thursday challenging the property-tax amendment ballot language Florida lawmakers approved for November.
cards.body:
A lawsuit filed Thursday in Leon County challenges the property-tax amendment Florida lawmakers approved for the November ballot. The complaint, filed by a voter advocacy group and two registered voters, argues the ballot language is "biased" and "misleading," accusing lawmakers of using campaign-style phrases like "Save Our Homes From Excessive Property Taxes," "protecting small businesses" and "ensuring fairness." The plaintiffs say the summary overstates the proposal by suggesting it guarantees funding for core services, fully eliminates non-school homestead taxes and immediately exempts the first $250,000 of a home's value, when the filing argues the initial exemption would be $150,000 in 2027. The lawsuit asks a judge to declare the wording unconstitutional and order Attorney General James Uthmeier to rewrite it within 10 days.

On June 2, lawmakers passed legislation to raise the homestead exemption for homeowners to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028 and create a framework for full exemption over time. Attorney Jamie Cole, representing the plaintiffs, argues the ballot language sounds like political advertising rather than a neutral summary. "A ballot amendment is supposed to be fair, neutral, and not biased, and it's supposed to be accurate," Cole said. Cole successfully challenged a similar property-tax amendment in 2007 when a judge found the ballot language for a proposed "Super Exemption" misleading. The amendment will appear on the November 2026 General Election Ballot and requires approval from at least 60 percent of voters to become law.

cards.headline: Fresh produce prices climb 6 percent forcing Treasure Coast families to adapt shopping habits
cards.teaser: Palm Beach County shoppers are changing how they buy groceries as fresh fruit and vegetable prices climbed more than 6 percent over the past year.
cards.body:
Palm Beach County shoppers are changing how they buy groceries as fresh fruit and vegetable prices climbed more than 6 percent over the past year, according to Thursday's federal inflation report and new consumer research. One in three American families now purchase fewer fresh fruits and vegetables due to rising costs, while 20 percent have switched to frozen alternatives, according to a new study from financial services company Advance America. One Palm Beach County shopper explained the appeal of frozen produce, saying the quality remains comparable and organic options are available at similar prices to fresh alternatives.

Some shoppers are expanding their grocery routines to find better deals on fresh produce. One Palm Beach County resident described his new approach, noting that his shopping day now consists of two or three stops, including a Don Victor's in Lake Worth for vegetables. Another shopper said prices have increased but remain manageable since she shops only for one person and buys fresh produce in moderate quantities. The Advance America study found Florida residents now spend over $28 more monthly on groceries compared to previous periods. Federal data shows overall grocery prices increased 2.7 percent year-over-year through May, with fresh produce leading the increases at more than 6 percent.

hero.headline: Oxbridge Academy hires Mike Colee as head football coach, roster numbers already growing
hero.body:
The Oxbridge Academy Thunderwolves football program has turned to new leadership as head coach Mike Colee takes the reins. Though only a few weeks into his role, Colee has already begun reshaping the team's roster. He acknowledged that when he arrived, the program faced lower enrollment numbers since families had already made summer plans before his involvement. However, the situation has shifted since he engaged with parents and students and released the schedule. "Once I got in there, once I got to meet with the parents, meet with the kids, get the schedule out there, we've been growing our numbers ever since," Colee said.

The new coach's approach is already resonating with players as the season approaches. Senior Cayden Pribramski highlighted Colee's emphasis on mental toughness and his ability to maximize each player's individual strengths. Rather than imposing a rigid system, Colee tailors his coaching to suit his athletes. "He's not the kind of guy to go out there and say, 'my way or the highway.' He's going to really build the stuff around you and help you to succeed," Pribramski explained. The senior believes this flexible approach will be key to the team's immediate success and long-term development as a program.

The Thunderwolves are determined to move forward after a challenging 0-11 campaign last season. Senior Brady Basis expressed the team's commitment to maintaining momentum as they prepare for the upcoming season. "We just want to keep working, keep going," Basis said. He pointed to a successful spring win as evidence that the team can build on positive performances. The goal is to carry that energy and winning mentality into the regular season.

Colee's appointment represents a significant turning point for Oxbridge Academy football. With improving roster numbers and players responding positively to his coaching philosophy, the program appears poised for change. The combination of increased participation and a coach who understands how to develop individual talent suggests the Thunderwolves are ready to compete under this new direction. As the team prepares to take the field, they're looking to prove themselves and leave last year's struggles behind.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie family travels to Boca Raton to watch Curaçao World Cup team train
cards.teaser: Fans from Port St. Lucie were among hundreds who filled Florida Atlantic University stadium in Boca Raton on Thursday to watch Curaçao's soccer team train before its first-ever World Cup appearance this weekend.
cards.body:
Hundreds of soccer fans gathered at Florida Atlantic University stadium in Boca Raton on Thursday to watch Curaçao's national team, known as the "Blue Wave," hold a training session ahead of their historic first-ever World Cup appearance. Among the supporters was Marionella Barzeycoggins, who traveled from Port St. Lucie with her family after learning about the event. "I found out they're gonna be in Boca and they have a training event. And I'm like, oh my God, I have to RSVP so we are here," Barzeycoggins said.

Curaçao, an island nation with a population of just over 150,000 people, is the smallest nation to qualify for the World Cup tournament and went undefeated in all 10 of its 2026 World Cup qualifying matches. Goalkeeper Eloy Room told WPTV the support has energized the team. "Really joyful to see that so many people showed up today — it gives us energy. We're really excited to start the World Cup," Room said. Midfielder Tahitch Chong added that the global recognition means everything to the island. Curaçao faces Germany this Sunday in Houston, Texas.

cards.headline: Wellington Soccer Club reports record 840 registrations as World Cup excitement builds
cards.teaser: More than 840 children have registered to play with the Wellington Soccer Club for the upcoming season, a record turnout that coaches and organizers attribute to growing World Cup excitement across South Florida.
cards.body:
The Wellington Soccer Club has reached a record enrollment of more than 840 children for the upcoming season, a surge organizers attribute to growing World Cup excitement across South Florida. At Greenview Shores Park, boys and girls are training with professional aspirations. Nine-year-old Parker said he wants to emulate Argentinian soccer star Tadeo Allende, who plays for Inter Miami. Patrick Zoete, the club's director of coaching, has taught soccer for more than 25 years and said the spike in registrations follows a pattern that repeats every four years as the World Cup approaches.

Zoete emphasized that soccer offers young players benefits beyond athletic development. "Soccer provides not only exercise but also a way of life for the kids to be part of a team, camaraderie. Some of them remain friends for life," he said. Zoete noted the area's advantage in having Messi at Inter Miami, allowing fans to watch the best player in the world. For Parker, the appeal extends beyond professional dreams. "Spending time with my friends. I meet new people every year. Every time we have a game, I'm really excited," Parker said of what draws him back each season.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County deputy accuses Lake Worth woman of holding phone with hand she doesn't have
cards.teaser: A Palm Beach County deputy pulled over Katie Thomas of Lake Worth for allegedly holding her phone in her right hand while driving, but Thomas was born without a right hand.
cards.body:
A Palm Beach County deputy pulled over Lake Worth resident Katie Thomas for allegedly holding her phone in her right hand while driving. The traffic stop became notable because Thomas was born without a right hand. Body camera footage shows the deputy telling Thomas, "You drove past me, holding the phone with your right hand, manipulating that phone. I mean, I saw you." Thomas responded by raising her arm to show her stump. When the deputy pressed further, asking if she had her phone in her hand, Thomas repeatedly replied "Hand to God" that she did not.

The citation was dropped for lack of evidence. The traffic stop has generated 110 million views on social media. Thomas, who has spent her life as an adaptive athlete raising awareness for the limb-difference community, said the viral attention stemmed from "literally being accused of something that I did not have a limb to be accused of." The Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office said an agency review of the case is underway. Thomas said she harbors no ill will toward the sheriff's office and has started selling "Hand to God" merchandise on Instagram, with proceeds benefiting Shriners Children's Hospital. She said she has no plans to sue.

cards.headline: White Sox move atop AL Central with 2-1 win over Braves behind Davis Martin's pitching
cards.teaser: Davis Martin worked six scoreless innings as the White Sox moved atop the AL Central with a 2-1 win over the Braves.
cards.body:
Martin's strong performance on the mound helped the White Sox take sole possession of first place in the American League Central division. The right-hander shut down the Braves offense through six innings, allowing the White Sox to secure the narrow victory.

The win gives the White Sox momentum as they continue their push for the division title. Martin's six scoreless frames provided the pitching stability the team needed to edge past the Braves in the low-scoring affair.

hero.headline: Humane Society thrift stores in Stuart house cats during Palm City shelter renovation
hero.body:
The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast is making creative use of its thrift stores to maintain animal care operations while undergoing major construction at its Palm City shelter. The nonprofit started building upgrades to its adoption, customer service, and intake areas earlier this year, and many of the organization's cats have been temporarily relocated to the two retail locations. According to spokesperson Sarah Fisher, this arrangement has proven essential while the shelter's regular cages remain unavailable during the renovation project.

The shift has transformed the thrift stores into dual-purpose spaces where visitors can browse donated merchandise while also meeting cats available for adoption. Senior Manager Kelly Ellis emphasized that every purchase made at either location directly supports the animals in the organization's care. The stores welcome donations of gently used items from the community, giving shoppers a way to contribute to both the animal rescue mission and the renovation efforts simultaneously. This approach has created an unexpected benefit by bringing adoptable pets into spaces where community members shop regularly.

Beyond the cats staying at the thrift store locations, the Humane Society is actively recruiting temporary foster homes for other animals affected by the construction. This multi-pronged approach allows the organization to continue its full range of services even as the facility undergoes necessary improvements. Animal shelters across the country face similar challenges when buildings require upgrades, but the Treasure Coast shelter's strategy demonstrates how creative problem-solving can maintain community engagement while addressing infrastructure needs.

The two thrift stores are located at 3302 SE Federal Highway in Stuart and 1099 NW 21st St, also in Stuart. Anyone interested in shopping, donating items, or learning about foster opportunities can visit hstc1.org for store hours and donation guidelines. Fisher noted that the stores have become a lifeline for the animals during this renovation period, allowing the nonprofit to continue its mission without interruption despite the temporary limitations on shelter space.

cards.headline: Delray Beach Public Library offers free STREAM programs and daily lunches for kids this summer
cards.teaser: The Delray Beach Public Library is running free Science, Technology, Reading, Art, Engineering and Math programs for kids and teens, plus free daily lunch for youth up to 18.
cards.body:
The Delray Beach Public Library is making summer brighter for kids and teens with free STREAM programs — Science, Technology, Reading, Art, Engineering and Math — open to all Florida residents. Kae Jonsons, director of development and community relations, said the library has been serving the community since 1913, when 30 women from the Ladies Improvement Society each donated a book to start the collection. Today, it welcomes more than 193,000 visitors annually to its 36,000-square-foot facility at Atlantic Avenue and Swinton Avenue.

Natalie Baron, young adult librarian, is leading sessions like ColorSpace: Artistic Excavations, where teens explore art history from cave paintings to ancient pottery. Teens can also join lab-based activities, including collaborative 3D puzzle builds, and pick up themed book boxes. Mandy Fulop, head of the children's department, is launching the STREAM Into Summer Literacy Program, encouraging young readers to set goals with librarians, track progress, and take home an Unearth a Story bag with a free STREAM book and activities. In partnership with the School District of Palm Beach County, the library serves free lunch daily from 11:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m., and snacks from 2 p.m. to 4 p.m., to youth up to 18. Family Nights on select Tuesdays invite children 5 and up to explore STREAM topics together.

hero.headline: Florida Judicial Qualifications Commission investigates 4th Circuit Judge for bench comments to litigants
hero.body:
The Florida Judicial Qualifications Commission has determined there is probable cause to investigate Circuit Court Judge Eric Roberson of the Florida 4th Judicial Circuit over allegedly inappropriate statements he made while presiding over cases. Roberson, who was appointed by Gov. Rick Scott and elected without opposition two years ago, is now facing scrutiny for his courtroom comments in multiple matters.

In the case of Zoe Wood v. Tatyana Ussin, Roberson allegedly told the respondent: "This is scary, there's something seriously off with you and it's a shock that there haven't been criminal charges for this. Part of me wants to ban you from ever coming back to our state, and keep your issues up in Virginia." The ruling in that case was successfully appealed, and a different judge was assigned to rehear it. In Taheshanoel Knight v. Matthew Kepp, the JQC says Roberson determined the petitioner lacked evidence to support her stalking allegations against the respondent. According to the commission, Roberson made comments to the petitioner about mental health issues and her name, stating that the court would eventually stop her from filing in the system.

The most serious allegations involve the case of Sylverter Greene v. Erika Greene-Raines. The JQC says Roberson called the petitioner "an entitled little snot" and told the respondent: "You are a terrible human being, and I can look you in the eye and tell you that. And I'm a judge, so that's a legal judgment, you are a terrible human being." The commission also alleges Roberson made remarks about the respondent's lack of violence while making comments that encouraged additional conflict between the parties. Roberson granted a permanent injunction against the respondent in this case and noted it was only his third such injunction that year, comparing the respondent to a previous respondent who had been a child molester.

Roberson has 20 days from June 11 to respond in writing to the JQC's findings. He has not responded to attempts to reach him at his office or cell phone, nor did he provide comment to Florida Politics about the allegations. When appointed nine years ago, Roberson, a former prosecutor in the same circuit, stated he would transition from an advocate's role to serving as a neutral arbiter. The JQC's findings suggest his conduct in these cases may not reflect that commitment to judicial neutrality.

cards.headline: Two Republicans enter race for Lake Worth Beach House District 89 seat, targeting Democratic incumbent
cards.teaser: Former Atlantis Mayor Cathy Higgins and businessman Jeff Buongiorno filed Thursday to challenge freshman Democratic Rep. Debra Tendrich in one of the most competitive districts in Florida.
cards.body:
Two Republicans have filed to challenge freshman Democratic Rep. Debra Tendrich in House District 89, ending an uncontested re-election bid for the Lake Worth Beach lawmaker in one of the state's most competitive districts. Cathy Higgins, a former Atlantis City Council member and the city's first woman mayor, and Jeff Buongiorno, a businessman and repeat candidate, both filed Thursday, one day before qualifying closed Friday. The district, rated D+1 according to MCI Maps, covers Greenacres, Lake Worth Beach, Lake Clarke Shores and Palm Springs. Tendrich won the seat by 2 percentage points in 2024. Higgins served on the Atlantis City Council from 2008 to 2020 and runs a security and valet company with her husband. She is expected to draw institutional support from incoming House Speaker Sam Garrison and the Florida House Republican Campaign Committee. Buongiorno previously ran for Congress and Palm Beach County Supervisor of Elections and has described himself as a political outsider with experience in law enforcement, technology, vocational education, transportation and manufacturing.

Tendrich's first term was defined by a landmark domestic violence reform package that passed both chambers unanimously and was signed by the governor. The bill strengthened protections for survivors, enhanced penalties for repeat offenders, increased victim relocation assistance and established a GPS monitoring pilot program. Criminal Justice Subcommittee Chair Danny Alvarez, a Republican, called Tendrich the "honey badger of representatives" for her persistence. She has raised just over $38,000 this cycle and secured backing from the Florida Police Benevolent Association, the Florida Fraternal Order of Police, Palm Beach County Professional Firefighters and Paramedics Local 2928 and the AFL-CIO.

cards.headline: Lake County Commissioner Anthony Sabatini suspends congressional campaign, cites resign-to-run law
cards.teaser: Lake County Commissioner Anthony Sabatini has dropped his campaign to succeed retiring U.S. Rep. Daniel Webster in Congress, marking the second time in two election cycles the controversial Republican has backed out of a federal run.
cards.body:
Lake County Commissioner Anthony Sabatini has dropped his campaign to succeed retiring U.S. Rep. Daniel Webster in Congress, marking the second time in two election cycles he has backed out of a federal run. Sabatini cited Florida's resign-to-run law and loyalty to another candidate, former Property Appraiser Carey Baker, in his decision. Sabatini wrote on X that qualifying to run for Congress would require him to immediately resign from the Lake County Commission. He also noted that he filed a lawsuit to challenge the resign-to-run law as unconstitutional, but the legal challenge could not be fully heard and decided before the qualifying deadline. A judge this month ruled that Sabatini would have to comply with the law that has been in Florida statutes for decades.

Sabatini won election to the Lake County Commission two years ago by unseating incumbent Doug Shields in a Republican Primary. He cited loyalty to Baker, who announced his candidacy after Sabatini. Baker was a political mentor to Sabatini when the younger Republican served as an Eustis City Council member and won election to the Florida House. Sabatini stated that he and Baker would have split too many votes within Lake County to be competitive in the larger primary race. Other candidates already qualified for the Republican Primary in Florida's 11th Congressional District include physician Nizam Razack, air conditioning business owner Joe Strada and comedian Tim Wilkins.

cards.headline: Democrat Karla Kemp transfers congressional campaign to Florida Senate District 18 race
cards.teaser: Democrat Karla Kemp is leaving the crowded race for Florida's 13th Congressional District and transferring her campaign to Senate District 18, where St. Petersburg Republican incumbent Sen. Nick DiCeglie is running for re-election.
cards.body:
Democrat Karla Kemp is leaving the crowded race for Florida's 13th Congressional District and transferring her campaign to Senate District 18, where St. Petersburg Republican incumbent Sen. Nick DiCeglie is running for re-election. The transfer was made official in a hand-delivered letter to the Florida Division of Elections late Thursday afternoon, though she did not qualify for the race at that time. Democrat Linda Kellis Harris has already filed and qualified for the race, meaning Kemp's transfer would force a Democratic Primary for the nomination if Kemp qualifies before the deadline.

The transfer comes after Leela Gray has quickly risen to front-runner status in the CD 13 Democratic Primary with significant establishment support and financial backing. Kemp's departure narrows the Democratic field in that race, though it remains crowded as Democrats look to challenge Republican U.S. Rep. Anna Paulina Luna in November. Kemp is a former paramedic and firefighter with experience in the medical field, health care and property insurance. DiCeglie was first elected to the Senate in 2022 after serving in the Florida House. He has not been challenged by a Republican candidate as of Friday morning, hours before the qualifying period ends. The winner of the Democratic Primary on Aug. 18 would advance to face DiCeglie in the November General Election.

cards.headline: Republican Rep. Susan Plasencia will not seek re-election in Seminole and Orange County House District 37
cards.teaser: Susan Plasencia said she is not seeking re-election for House District 37 representing Seminole and Orange counties, citing her commitment to caring for her mother in the final stages of Alzheimers disease.
cards.body:
Republican Rep. Susan Plasencia announced Friday that she will not seek re-election for House District 37 representing Seminole and Orange counties. In a letter, Plasencia wrote that her mother is in the final stages of Alzheimer's disease and that she and her siblings are committed to caring for her at home with dignity. Plasencia is the sister of former Rep. Rene "Coach P" Plasencia and was first elected in 2022 by defeating then-Rep. Carlos Guillermo Smith in a surprise upset. Smith later won a Senate seat. In 2024, Plasencia narrowly won re-election over Democrat Nate Douglas, who had out-fundraised her. She currently serves as Executive Director of Orlando Regional Foundation.

Republican Robert Prater switched races late Thursday afternoon to run for Plasencia's seat after previously running for House District 43. Prater would have faced a tough test in HD 43 from Democrat Samuel Vilchez Santiago, who raised $158,000 and has the support of the Democratic establishment after serving as Orange County Democratic Chair. Plasencia's political committee gave Prater $1,000 in January, his first campaign donation as an HD 43 candidate. Prater's opponent in HD 37 is Democrat Jane Aman, a lecturer at the University of Central Florida and former English teacher for Seminole County's Crooms Academy. Plasencia endorsed Prater in her announcement letter.

cards.headline: Florida CD 16 Republican debate set for July 31 with Gruters, Speir and Pope
cards.teaser: A debate between Sydney Gruters, Eddie Speir and Ed Pope is now set for July 31, giving Republican voters in Florida's 16th Congressional District a chance to see the full GOP field side-by-side before the August Primary.
cards.body:
A hotly awaited debate between Sydney Gruters, Eddie Speir and Ed Pope is now set, giving Republican voters in Florida's 16th Congressional District a chance to see the full GOP field side-by-side before the August Primary. The Republican Women's Club of Sarasota will host the July 31 debate at Michael's On East in Sarasota, with doors opening at 11 a.m. and the program starting at noon. The trio are running to replace retiring U.S. Rep. Vern Buchanan. Speir and Pope have pushed for a direct debate with Gruters, who accepted this week. The club is billing the debate as the culmination of its 2026 Candidate Series and will use a question-and-answer format to give candidates a chance to share their vision and priorities. The group expects an audience of 200 to 300 or more attendees, including Republican voters, activists, volunteers, donors and community leaders.

Gruters has been endorsed by President Donald Trump, U.S. House Speaker Mike Johnson, U.S. Rep. Anna Paulina Luna and several conservative organizations, including Maggie's List, Winning for Women, Value In Electing Women PAC and Turning Point Action. She has also swept endorsements from sheriffs in all six neighboring counties. Gruters previously served as Executive Director of the New College Foundation, District Director for U.S. Rep. Greg Steube and State Director for USDA Rural Development in Florida and the U.S. Virgin Islands under Trump. Speir is the founder of Bradenton-based Inspiration Academy and previously built and sold the financial software company Mortgage Cadence. Pope is a Navy veteran and former Florida Highway Patrol trooper. The Republican Primary is scheduled for Aug. 18.

cards.headline: Former Mississippi Rep. Mike Ezell endorses Bea Valenti in crowded Florida CD 14 Republican Primary
cards.teaser: Bea Valenti picked up a congressional endorsement in her bid for CD 14 from Mike Ezell, the Mississippi Republican and Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation Subcommittee Chairman she once worked for as a senior adviser.
cards.body:
Bea Valenti secured a congressional endorsement from Mike Ezell, the Mississippi Republican and Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation Subcommittee Chairman she previously worked for as a senior adviser. Ezell, a former Jackson County Sheriff now in his second term, praised Valenti as a Trump alumna and America First patriot, calling her the best candidate to defeat Rep. Kathy Castor. "Bea worked for me as a top senior advisor, where she helped deliver wins for our district and I watched firsthand how tirelessly she worked to help us advance an America First agenda," Ezell said. He noted that her commitment to her hometown and home county were evident.

Valenti, a fourth-generation Hillsborough County native and former Trump Administration official, called Ezell someone who understands fighting for constituents and delivering results. Her campaign credits her work in Ezell's office with advancing FEMA reforms and securing more than $70 million for defense and infrastructure projects across the Gulf Coast. The endorsement adds credibility to Valenti's candidacy in a crowded Republican Primary. She also has backing from retiring U.S. Rep. Neal Dunn and VIEW PAC. Valenti faces Tampa technology executive Kevin Steele, the early financial front-runner; former state Rep. Mike Beltran; and 2024 GOP nominee Rocky Rochford. The Aug. 18 Primary winner will face Castor, the 20-year incumbent, in a district redrawn to favor Republicans.

hero.headline: Hundreds of fish found dead in Port St. Lucie community after city algae treatment
hero.teaser: Hundreds of dead fish floated on the water at the Sawgrass Lakes community in Port St.
hero.body:
Dead fish floated on the water at the Sawgrass Lakes community in Port St. Lucie on Thursday following an algae treatment conducted earlier in the week. Neighbors discovered dead fish in their backyards Thursday morning and shared videos with WPTV. Resident Jim Herbert said there were hundreds and hundreds of fish and thousands of smaller ones gulping air. The city hired vendor SOLitude to treat the water for algae on Tuesday and Wednesday. According to experts, high heat combined with algae treatment can make water uninhabitable for aquatic life. On Thursday, crews removed dead fish and tested oxygen levels in the water. Herbert noted this was at least the second fish die-off since living in the neighborhood.

Scott Samples with the city of Port St. Lucie said the city has been working with neighbors and other cities and counties to find solutions and hopes there might be a couple of options soon, though those are dependent on several factors. Jim Moir, executive director of the Indian Riverkeeper, suggested the city look at more natural solutions including planting aquatic vegetation, reducing fertilizer use, and removing sediment that fuels algae growth. Moir said the city will end up in a cycle it cannot break unless it goes back to square one and starts with natural remediation.

cards.teaser: Palm Beach County shoppers are changing how they buy groceries as fresh fruit and vegetable prices climbed more than 6% over the past year, according to Thursday's federal inflation report and new consumer research.
cards.body:

hero.headline: C.H. Robinson and White Hawk Carriers named in St. Lucie County Turnpike crash lawsuit
hero.teaser: C.H. Robinson Company Inc., described as one of the largest transportation brokers in the United States, is named as a defendant in a wrongful death lawsuit stemming from a fatal Turnpike crash in St. Lucie County.
hero.body:
A wrongful death lawsuit was filed following a fatal crash on Florida's Turnpike that killed three people when a commercial truck driver attempted an illegal U-turn. On August 12, 2025, at approximately 2:57 p.m., truck driver Harjinder Singh attempted to make a U-turn through a clearly marked median crossover near Mile Marker 171 in St. Lucie County that was designated for official use only. The 53-foot trailer swung across and blocked all northbound travel lanes. A minivan driven by Herby Dufresne and carrying passengers Rodrigue Dor and Faniola Joseph struck the left side of the trailer in what the complaint describes as a fatal underride crash. All three occupants were killed. The lawsuit, filed by an attorney representing the estate of victim Faniola Joseph, names multiple defendants including the truck driver, White Hawk Carriers Inc., C.H. Robinson, and company manager Harpreet Singh.

The complaint raises serious questions about the truck driver's qualifications. According to the lawsuit, Harjinder Singh was present in the United States without lawful immigration status and without authorization to work. Despite this alleged status, Singh obtained a Class A California commercial driver's license, which the complaint states was issued in violation of applicable federal and state regulations. The lawsuit further alleges Singh lacked required English language proficiency under federal regulations that mandate commercial drivers must read and speak English sufficiently to understand highway signs and respond to official inquiries.

Before C.H. Robinson selected White Hawk Carriers to transport the load, the trucking company had already accumulated a documented unsafe federal safety record, according to the complaint. This record included a prior reportable crash in December 2024, multiple roadside inspection citations for unsafe driving violations including speeding and improper lane changes, repeated hours-of-service violations with falsified duty status records, and vehicle defects including brake problems and air-brake leaks. The complaint alleges this safety information was publicly available through the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration's Safety Measurement System. C.H. Robinson, described as one of the largest transportation brokers in the United States with headquarters in Eden Prairie, Minnesota, and eight Florida offices, marketed itself as a company that properly vets carriers using federal safety data but allegedly failed to do so in this case.

The lawsuit names Harpreet Singh, identified as a White Hawk Carriers manager and California resident, individually as a defendant. The complaint alleges he was personally responsible for hiring, training, and supervising company drivers, including Harjinder Singh, and failed to adequately investigate the truck driver's immigration status, work authorization, English proficiency, and overall fitness before hiring. Additionally, an unauthorized passenger identified as Harneet Singh was in the truck cab at the time of the crash, representing violations of safety standards and federal motor carrier regulations. The lawsuit seeks damages exceeding $75,000 under Florida's Wrongful Death Act.

cards.headline: Hundreds of fish die in Port St. Lucie neighborhood after city algae treatment

cards.body:
Dead fish were floating on the water at Sawgrass Lakes community in Port St. Lucie on Thursday following an algae treatment earlier in the week. Neighbors shared video of dead fish found in their backyards Thursday morning. "There were hundreds and hundreds of fish here, and thousands of those little ones just gulping the air," said neighbor Jim Herbert. Jerry Cook, another resident, said he does not think the issue is an overnight fix or a couple months fix, but rather a few years fix.

The city hired vendor SOLitude to treat the water for algae on Tuesday and Wednesday. Experts told WPTV that with high heat and algae treatment, the water can become uninhabitable for aquatic life. On Thursday, crews removed dead fish and tested oxygen levels in the water. Herbert noted this is at least the second fish die-off since he has lived there. Scott Samples with the city of Port St. Lucie said they have been working with neighbors and other cities and counties to find solutions, hoping options might become available soon. Jim Moir, executive director of the Indian Riverkeeper, recommended the city look at natural solutions like planting aquatic vegetation, reducing fertilizer use, and removing sediment that fuels algae growth. Moir said the community will end up in a cycle it cannot break unless it returns to square one and starts with natural remediation.
